title: Give better instructions
summary: Turn a vague goal into a precise, ordered algorithm that a machine can follow.

scenario.briefing: A campus courier robot understands only the commands you place in its queue. Order the commands so it delivers a parcel without knocking anything over.

objectives.description: Check understanding through the remaining explanation and transfer evidence.

hints: Think about what the robot must hold before it can move.
A safe delivery starts by picking up the parcel and ends by returning to the charger.
Pick up, turn, walk, lower, return. Put the movement in the middle.
The sequence is: lift the parcel, turn right, walk forward, lower the parcel, return to the charger.

misconceptions.feedback: A robot cannot deliver what it is not holding. Acquire the parcel before moving.

misconceptions.description: Believing a high-level goal is a precise instruction.
misconceptions.feedback: "Deliver the parcel" states an outcome, not the steps. A machine needs unambiguous operations in a workable order.

sections.title: Algorithms are precise
sections.body: An algorithm is a finite sequence of unambiguous steps that solves a problem. The courier robot knows how to lift, turn, walk, lower, and return, but it does not know what delivery means. You supply the order and the details.

sections.title: Order carries meaning
sections.body: The same set of commands in a different order can produce a broken result. Ordering is part of the algorithm, not decoration. Later you will see that programs are algorithms expressed in a language a computer can execute.

vocabulary.definition: A finite, precise sequence of steps for solving a problem.
Open to more than one interpretation.
Carrying out the steps of an algorithm.

steps.title: Load the courier queue
steps.prompt: Arrange these commands so the courier delivers the parcel safely. Use the up and down buttons or drag with a pointer.

items.label: Lift the parcel from the loading shelf
Lower the parcel at the delivery desk

steps.explanation: The courier must hold the parcel before moving, travel to the desk, release the parcel, and then return.

steps.title: Which instruction is precise?
steps.prompt: A new courier has no shared assumptions about the campus. Choose the instruction it can execute without guessing.

quiz.prompt: Which command is precise enough for a machine?
quiz.explanation: Walk forward 4 steps names an action and a measurable amount. The other commands depend on judgment the robot does not have.

hints: Which command has a measurable action?
Look for a number and a direction.
Walk forward 4 steps is actionable. Quickly and carefully are not measurable here.
The precise command is walk forward 4 steps.

steps.title: Why order matters
steps.prompt: Select every statement that is true about algorithms.

statements.label: An algorithm should finish after a finite number of steps.
The order of steps never changes the result.
Each step should be unambiguous to its executor.
An algorithm is any random sequence of actions.

steps.explanation: Algorithms are finite, precise, and order-sensitive. Reordering operations can change or break the result.

accessibility.summary: Reordering works with buttons as well as pointer dragging, and the current order is available as text.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Focus an item and use the move up and move down buttons. Drag and drop is optional.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: Each item announces its position, such as item 2 of 5, and the final order is read after each move.
